# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

First iteration off the seed (LEDGER shows baseline only). Reward is HARD scoring:
each task ships 3 test-case input files and the agent's extracted solution code is
re-run on all 3 (adapter `spreadsheetbench/adapter.py:1241-1242` string-replaces the
`1_<id>_input.xlsx` filename with `2_/3_` and re-executes). Reward = 1.0 iff all 3
match, so 2/3 = reward 0. This mechanism is the key to the dominant failure class.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Non-generalizing code (hardcoded literals) | 56561 (hardcoded `{5:0,6:0,7:16,...}`), 34-5 (hardcoded cutoff `date(2023,12,1)`), most 0/3 + all 2/3 partials (267-18, 250-20) | Agent inspects test-case 1 then bakes observed values/counts/positions/dates into the solution; those literals are wrong on the 2 hidden inputs → fails ≥1 of 3 | KNOWLEDGE (agent cannot know code is re-run on other inputs) | add missing rule grounded in the re-execution harness + structural self-check |
| 2 | Code/formula recipe written as text, not executed | 269-44, 254-34 (pasted VBA source into A1:A15 / C2) | Instruction phrased "write a macro/VBA/script"; agent writes the SOURCE CODE into cells instead of performing the transformation on the data | KNOWLEDGE / output-contract | tighten output contract ("produce the result, not the recipe") |
| 3 | Stops before genuinely verifying / generalizing | many "Done" after one write | Template's step-3 verify is optional advice; agent inspects once and finishes without checking values or generality | BEHAVIORAL-skippable → fix with STRUCTURE | ordered procedure with verify as a precondition to finishing |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | add missing rule (grounded in source) | prompt.md | New "WRITE GENERAL CODE" block: solution is re-run on 2 hidden inputs with same layout/different data; derive every value/count/index/date from the input at run time; never hardcode preview-observed literals; resolve "today/current month" from runtime date; instruction-stated constants are OK. General policy, no task specifics. | Yes — the 51 passing tasks already generalize (11 use formulas, which inherently generalize); this only forbids a behavior none of them do (hardcoding). |
| 2 | tighten output contract | prompt.md | New "PRODUCE THE RESULT, NOT THE RECIPE" block: perform the described macro/VBA/formula operation and write resulting values; never paste VBA/macro/script source into cells; a correct spreadsheet FORMULA is explicitly still allowed (grader recalculates). | Yes — no passing task pastes code-as-text; formulas kept legal so the 11 formula-passers are unaffected. |
| 3 | ordered procedure / checklist (structure) | task_template.md | Rewrote the interaction section into ordered steps INSPECT → SOLVE (derive-from-input) → VERIFY (re-open, recompute one by hand, confirm nothing hardcoded) as a precondition of replying with no code block. | Yes — passing tasks already inspect/solve/verify; adding a checklist doesn't change their final artifact, only makes the skip-path unavailable. |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)
- Cluster 1 / trace 56561: solution wrote `values = {5:0,6:0,7:16,13,12,11,10,12}` copied from case-1 inspection → new rule "NEVER hardcode a value/count/answer observed in the preview; write the loop that DERIVES them", with the exact `values = {...}` counter-example, so the agent writes data-driven logic that survives cases 2/3. Verified against harness re-execution at adapter.py:1241-1242.
- Cluster 1 / trace 34-5: solution set `cutoff = date(2023, 12, 1)` read from the sample → new clause "resolve today/current-month from `datetime.now()`, never a fixed date from the sample" makes the cutoff data/runtime-driven.
- Cluster 2 / trace 269-44 & 254-34: agent wrote VBA `Sub …` lines into A1:A15 / C2 → contract line "actually PERFORM the transformation and write resulting values; never paste VBA/macro/script source into cells" would have made it delete the rows and write the resulting column values instead of code text.
- Cluster 3 / traces ending "Done" after a single write: verify is now step 3 and a stated precondition of finishing ("Reply with NO code block only after step 3 passes"), turning an optional suggestion into an ordered gate.
- SAFE check for the reframed literals/formula guidance: enumerated the 11 passing formula-writers (37962, 49237, 50682, 2212, 31420, 32255, 35747, 37086, 44264, 45581, 54675) — the new text keeps formulas explicitly legal, so none flip; literal-computing passers keep computing literals; only hardcoding (which no passer does) is newly forbidden. Behaviorally no passing task changes.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees: serial (single-context) — diagnosis was fast via direct trace inspection + reading the adapter/inference source to confirm the 3-input re-execution mechanism; fan-out not needed.
- Prior iterations: none — LEDGER/JOURNAL show baseline only; RUNMAP empty. Nothing to build on or avoid re-trying yet.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- The generalization rule (cluster 1) is the load-bearing fix; keep it. Do NOT re-add any
  wording that PREFERS literals over formulas or discourages formulas — the passing set proves
  formulas are a winning, generalizing strategy.
- Keep formulas explicitly permitted; only VBA/macro/script SOURCE text in cells is banned.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 267-18 (2/3): yellow-highlight detection misses theme-colored fills on case 3 — a task-specific
  color-encoding edge, not a general prose rule; risky to over-specify. Left for a targeted fix.
- 55912: agent hand-wrote fragile shared-string XML parsing (filter/pivot task) — behavioral
  over-engineering, not a knowledge gap prose can close.
- 45300 / similar interpretation-ambiguity tasks ("delete from where 'FT' appears" — keep or drop
  the marker?): genuine spec ambiguity, no general rule that isn't a guess.
- Relative-date semantics beyond the datetime.now clause (exact frozen reference date) is
  undeterminable from the traces; not fixed further.
